newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus fixes rouble at 22,050, corridor scrapped.
newsitem.headline: Belarus fixes rouble at 22,050, corridor scrapped.

text.p: Belarus scrapped its currency corridor on Monday and fixed its rouble slightly lower at 22,050 to the dollar plus or minus 1.5 percent, First Deputy Prime Minister Pyotr Prokopovich told a news conference.
"We have made a single rate for the stock exchange, the interbank (market) and for cash deals -- that is the main aim of the decision," he said.

The unit was quoted at around 29,000 units per U.S. dollar on the interbank market on Monday, and the move was likely to depress Western economists who want credit-starved Belarus to liberalise its currency policy.
"There are big things worrying the World Bank and above all the reintroduction of a free currency market," Christopher Willoughby of Minsk's World Bank office said on Friday.
But Prokopovich said the move was designed to create a single exchange rate and added: "The less we talk about currency regulation, the better for our economy."
The International Monetary Fund has sent a fact-finding staff visit to Minsk but no talks are planned on renewing a $300 million stand-by loan most of which was frozen last year.
